violation_type.title: Diapering Procedures-Soiled Diapers Kept in a Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3505(f))
violation_type.short_title: Diapering Procedures-Soiled Diapers Kept in a Sanitary Manner
violation_type.typical_finding: Although there is a trashcan with a lid used for diapers, several diapers were observed in another trashcan without a lid accessible to children.    NOTE: The toddler caregiver changed out the trashcan and started using the other trashcan with a lid used for diapers.

finding_variants.text: Although there is a trashcan with a lid used for diapers, several diapers were observed in another trashcan without a lid accessible to children.    NOTE: The toddler caregiver changed out the trashcan and started using the other trashcan with a lid used for diapers.
An infant and toddler classroom both had soiled diapers in the trash can without a lid. This was corrected at inspection.
During the monitoring inspection it was observed that the dirty diapers in the toddler bathroom were being stored in an uncovered container.

Soiled diapers were observed in a trash can with no lid in a pre-k room restroom.        Note: This was CORRECTED during inspection as a trash can with a lid was obtained and placed in the children's restroom.
The trash can in the Pre-K restroom did not have a lid and contained soiled diapers that were not sealed in bags.
A soiled pull-up was observed in a trash can without a lid. The soiled pull-up was also not in a sealed plastic bag.

Diapering Procedures-Soiled Diapers Kept in a Sanitary Manner: In one restroom observed a soiled diaper/pull-up in a trash can without a lid that was not in a sealed plastic bag. You must cover containers used for soiled diapers or keep them in a sanitary manner, such as placing soiled diapers in individual sealed bags. This was corrected at inspection as staff transferred the trash bag to a trash can with a lid.
